financials.source: UCLA Health generated more than $4.4 billion in operating revenue in FY2024-25 and ended with a positive net position of $284 million (Daily Bruin reporting on November 2025 UC Regents Health Services Committee meeting). The UC Regents FY2025 budget projected UCLA Hospital System operating revenue at $4,752 million. A September 2026 Regents document reports UCLA Health modified net income of $780 million (15.5% modified net margin), but the fiscal year was cut off in the source. Patient volume increased 11.9% year-over-year. UCLA campus total assets (including health system) were $20.1 billion in FY2023; no standalone UCLA Health balance sheet is published — audited financials exist only at the UC system level. UCLA Health's FY2024 campus-wide operating loss was $144.2 million, a reversal from $159.6 million operating income the prior year (campus-wide, not health system only). Precise UCLA Health-only audited figures are in the UC Medical Centers Annual Financial Report 2024-25 (Tables MDA.24a-c), not available via web search.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: UCLA Health's investments are managed at the University of California system level. The UC system-wide endowment totaled $29.5 billion as of June 30, 2024 (UC Investments). UCLA's campus share of the endowment is estimated at approximately $3.5 billion (third-party aggregator, June 2024); the UCLA Investment Company manages UCLA Foundation endowment and other assets. UCLA Foundation approved spending policy for FY2024 is 4.25% of a 12-quarter rolling average. Most endowment funds participate in the General Endowment Pool (GEP), a balanced portfolio of equities, fixed-income, and alternative investments. UCLA campus standalone financial records do not fully reflect centrally managed investment balances.
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: UCLA Health operates five hospitals across Southern California: Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center (446 beds, Westwood), UCLA Santa Monica Medical Center (281 beds), UCLA West Valley Medical Center (260 beds, acquired March 2024 from HCA Healthcare on a 14-acre campus), UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital (131 beds within Ronald Reagan/Santa Monica), and Resnick Neuropsychiatric Hospital (74 beds). The system also operates approximately 290 clinics and 12 immediate care locations across Southern California and the Central Coast. Real estate values are not separately disclosed; properties are owned by The Regents of the University of California.
balanceSheetWealth.notes: UCLA Health's balance sheet wealth is embedded within the University of California system, making it difficult to isolate. The UC system holds $29.5 billion in endowment assets and total system-wide assets of approximately $112 billion (FY2025). UCLA's campus-wide assets (health system plus academic) totaled $20.1 billion in FY2023. The health system benefits from university-wide investment returns, centralized treasury management, and the state's implicit backing. A behavioral health campus in mid-Wilshire Los Angeles is planned for 2026, representing additional capital investment.

bondDebt.largestIssue: University of California Medical Center Pooled Revenue Bonds (shared credit across five UC medical centers)
bondDebt.issuerAuthority: The Regents of the University of California (issuer); bonds also issued through California Health Facilities Financing Authority (CHFFA)
bondDebt.source: UCLA Health's debt is issued through the UC Medical Center Pooled Revenue Bond (MCPRB) program, which is a pooled credit secured by gross revenues of all five UC medical centers ($26.2 billion pledged revenues, FY2024-25). Total UC system bonds outstanding were approximately $32 billion as of April 30, 2025 across General Revenue Bond, Limited Project Revenue Bond, and MCPRB credits. All five UC medical centers combined had long-term debt of approximately $10.4 billion (FY2025 Medical Centers Report). UC issued approximately $4.9 billion in bonds in FY2024-25 over three transactions. UCLA's specific share of outstanding MCPRB debt is not separately disclosed. A 2022 UC medical center bond sale totaled approximately $3 billion (Moody's Aa3, S&P AA-, Fitch AA-).

relatedOrganizations.relatedPartyTransactions: UCLA Health president Johnese Spisso sits on the boards of Welltower Inc. (NYSE: WELL), a healthcare REIT that leases space to the University of California, and Vizient Inc., a group purchasing organization through which UCLA Health sources supplies. The San Francisco Chronicle reported these dual roles raise conflict-of-interest concerns. Spisso received $336,709 in total compensation as a Welltower director (2024 proxy). She previously served as a Douglas Emmett Inc. independent director (2019-2022). UC policy requires disclosure of outside activities but the Regents' conflict-of-interest review of these arrangements was not found in public records.

communityBenefit.source: UCLA Health's 340B program page reports $421.2 million 'provided as charity care, in-kind health services, volunteer time, health education training and cost of uncompensated care for Medi-Cal patients' (FY2024). This is a bundled figure — not pure charity care. An additional $306.5 million was reported as uncompensated care for Medicare patients (FY2024), bringing total claimed community benefit to approximately $727.7 million. However, UCLA Health's FY2019-20 community benefit report broke out financial assistance (charity care) at only $8,624,297 out of $619,583,422 total community benefit including Medicare — meaning pure charity care was approximately 0.2% of operating revenue. A separate UC report lists UCLA financial assistance at $28.6 million for FY2020, suggesting different category definitions. Under California's Hospital Fair Pricing Act (SB 1276), UCLA Health must offer charity care to patients at or below 400% of the Federal Poverty Level. UC Health system-wide delivered $5.9 billion in community benefits and uncompensated care in FY2023-24.

taxAdvantage.notes: UCLA Health operates under the tax-exempt status of The Regents of the University of California, a government instrumentality exempt under IRC 501(c)(3) since 1939. Tax advantages include: (1) exemption from federal and state income taxes on $4.4 billion+ in operating revenue; (2) property tax exemption on all hospital and clinic real estate across Southern California, including five hospitals and approximately 290 clinics; (3) access to tax-exempt bond financing through UC Medical Center Pooled Revenue Bonds (AA-/Aa3 rated), providing interest rate subsidies on billions in borrowing; (4) $133.4 million in 340B Drug Pricing Program savings (FY2024); and (5) ability to receive tax-deductible donations through the UCLA Foundation. As a public university health system, UCLA Health also receives state appropriations and benefits from the UC system's $29.5 billion endowment pool. The combined tax benefit likely exceeds hundreds of millions annually, but no comprehensive estimate has been published.

keyRiskFactors: Pooled bond credit: UCLA Health's bonds are part of the UC Medical Center Pooled Revenue Bond program securing all five UC medical centers — UCLA's individual creditworthiness is not separately rated
UC system total debt of approximately $32 billion as of April 2025, with $4.9 billion in new issuances in FY2024-25 alone
Campus-wide operating loss of $144.2 million in FY2024 (UCLA overall, not health system only), a sharp reversal from $159.6 million operating income the prior year
Nearly $700 million in sexual abuse lawsuit settlements (James Heaps cases) represent a massive financial and reputational liability
Rapid expansion via West Hills Hospital acquisition (March 2024) and planned behavioral health campus (2026) adds integration and capital risk
CEO holds board seats at Welltower (REIT that leases space to UC) and Vizient (group purchasing organization supplying UCLA Health), creating governance and conflict-of-interest risk
Dependence on state of California and UC system for fiscal support, bond guarantees, and investment management; state budget pressures can directly impact operations
340B savings of $133.4 million (FY2024) face legislative and manufacturer threats to the program nationally

program340B.source: UCLA Health 340B Community Health Program page (FY2024: $133.4 million in savings; FY2023: $123 million). HRSA 340B OPAIS database lists two DSH-eligible covered entities with child sites including Santa Clarita Radiation Oncology (DSH050262AZ, since April 2023) and Pain Medicine Procedure Unit (DSH050112H, since April 2025). UC's 2023 RFI response notes all UC hospitals have DSH adjustment percentages well above the minimum eligibility requirement. UCLA Health states savings fund services for under- and uninsured patients and costly therapies such as CAR-T cell treatments.

acquisitions.target: West Hills Hospital and Medical Center (from HCA Healthcare)
acquisitions.description: UCLA Health acquired the 260-bed West Hills Hospital and Medical Center in the San Fernando Valley from HCA Healthcare, with the transaction closing March 28, 2024. The hospital was renamed UCLA West Valley Medical Center. The acquisition was UCLA Health's first hospital in the San Fernando Valley and was driven by inpatient, emergency department, and operating room capacity constraints. The campus includes seven operating rooms and a freestanding ambulatory surgery center on a 14-acre site. UCLA retained the vast majority of staff. Purchase price was not disclosed.

legalIssues.description: The University of California system paid nearly $700 million total to settle lawsuits brought by more than 300 women who alleged sexual abuse by UCLA gynecologist James Heaps. A $374.4 million settlement was announced in 2022, on top of prior settlements. Heaps pleaded not guilty to 21 felony criminal counts. An earlier proposed class-action settlement would have paid between $2,500 and $250,000 each to up to 6,600 of Heaps' former patients.
legalIssues.source: Associated Press, Courthouse News, Daily Bruin

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: UCLA Health's investments are managed at the UC system level and cannot be isolated to the health system. The UC system-wide endowment totaled $29.5 billion as of June 2024. UCLA's campus share is estimated at approximately $3.5 billion. UCLA Health's modified net income was reported at $780 million (15.5% modified net margin) in a recent fiscal year, but the year and definition were not confirmed. The pooled nature of UC investments makes a health-system-specific ratio impossible to compute.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: UCLA Health's bond debt is embedded within the UC Medical Center Pooled Revenue Bond program (all five UC medical centers combined long-term debt approximately $10.4 billion, FY2025). UCLA's specific share is not disclosed. Using the $421.2 million bundled community benefit claim (FY2024), even one-fifth of the pooled debt (~$2.1 billion) would represent approximately 5x the claimed community benefit. Using the $8.6 million in pure financial assistance from FY2020, the ratio would be far more extreme.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: UCLA Health's FY2019-20 community benefit report listed financial assistance (charity care) at $8,624,297 out of $619,583,422 total community benefit — approximately 1.4% of community benefit and roughly 0.2% of operating revenue. A separate UC report lists UCLA financial assistance at $28.6 million for FY2020. The discrepancy may reflect different category definitions. Either figure — $8.6 million or $28.6 million — is a fraction of a percent of UCLA Health's $4.4 billion+ in annual operating revenue, and substantially less than the $133.4 million the system captures in 340B drug discount savings alone.

accusation: UCLA Health operates within the University of California's $29.5 billion endowment and a campus asset base exceeding $20 billion — yet its hospitals reported just $8.6 million in direct financial assistance (0.2% of revenue) in its most recent detailed breakdown, bundling that with $412 million in other categories to claim $421 million in 'community benefit' — while generating over $4.4 billion in annual operating revenue, capturing $133.4 million in 340B drug discount savings that exceed its charity care sixteen-fold, paying its president $2.6 million in total compensation while she collects an additional $336,709 sitting on the board of Welltower (a healthcare REIT that leases space to the University of California) and serves as a director of Vizient (the group purchasing organization through which UCLA Health sources supplies), financing expansion through tax-exempt UC Medical Center Pooled Revenue Bonds rated AA-/Aa3, settling nearly $700 million in sexual abuse lawsuits, and operating as a government instrumentality of the State of California exempt from federal income tax, state income tax, property tax, and sales tax on billions in revenue and real estate holdings across Southern California.
